groups.title: Battle over Europa
entries: The war has moved to Jupiter. Battles now rage 2,000 km above Europa, its cracked ice filling half the sky below you, with Jupiter hanging in the distance at its true size and the other Galilean moons strung along its orbital plane. Some battles are fought over volcanic Io or Ganymede instead. Every world is built from NASA maps at real scale.

Deep space finally looks like deep space: true black with crisp pin-point stars, and a tiny, blinding Sun. Sunlight bouncing off Europa now lights the underside of every ship, Jupiter casts a warm glow, and polished hulls reflect the moon and Jupiter around them. Your eyes also adapt: stare into the sunlit moon, the Sun or a close explosion and the battlefield dims, then slowly opens back up when you turn to the dark. Bloom and tone mapping were retuned so bright things glow without washing everything out.

All-new weapon and explosion effects: plasma bolts are white-hot streaks with a coloured sheath (and a blinding point when one is coming straight at you), rail shots leave rippling ion trails, missiles burn hot and leave sunlit smoke, and explosions flash, billow from white-hot to orange to dark soot, and throw glowing embers.

Shields ripple with hexagonal cells that light up as the impact spreads, capture zones are now subtle sensor fields around a real relay station with a rising fill and shimmering edge, and asteroids are dark cratered rock with sharp sunlit relief.

Star Battles has its own app icon: a Silverwing streaking past Jupiter and Io with its cannons blazing. It shows on your Android home screen (including Android 13+ themed icons) and on the Windows .exe, taskbar and window.

groups.title: Smoother flying and seeker locks
entries: New default mouse steering, Mouse Aim: move the mouse to place the reticle and your ship flies smoothly onto it without overshooting. Tiny mouse movements now make tiny, precise corrections. Prefer the old joystick style? Pick Virtual Stick in Settings › Controls.
Touch, gamepad and Virtual Stick steering now respond almost linearly, so small thumb movements turn the ship instead of doing nothing. Tune it with the new Stick response curve slider.

Light aim assist: when your aim is right next to an enemy's lead point, the reticle is gently pulled onto it and slows down slightly so you can track. Adjust it or switch it off with the Aim assist slider in Settings › Gameplay.

Seeker missiles are clearer: keep an enemy inside the lock brackets around your crosshair, watch the ring fill as the lock tone speeds up, then fire on LOCKED. The HUD tells you when you're locking, locked, reloading or dumb-firing, and locks no longer drop when two enemies are close together. Silverwing and Wraith now carry a seeker pod too.

F (or T, LB, or the new TARGET touch button) selects the enemy closest to your reticle; press again to step to the next. Your selected target is labelled and stays marked at the screen edge with its range, and seekers lock onto it first.

groups.title: Mothership Siege
entries: New mode: Mothership Siege. The IRON VANGUARD, a 1.5 km carrier bristling with sixteen flak and heavy cannon turrets, hangs off Saturn under a shield bubble. AEGIS flies escort, KRONOS brings it down. Pick a side from the new SIEGE tile on the home screen, or switch the mode in a multiplayer lobby.

Break the carrier in three stages: knock out the four shield generators, hammer the hull armour as breaches blow open and fires spread, then destroy the reactor once its shutters tear away. Attackers share a pool of reinforcements that grows each time a stage falls; defenders win if the clock runs out or the attack runs dry.
Watch it go: when the reactor fails, explosions race along the hull and the IRON VANGUARD breaks apart into burning sections. If the defenders hold, it lights its engines and jumps to warp.

Turrets track and lead you, so jink. Your HUD marks every generator, turret and the reactor, the radar shows the carrier's outline, and AI pilots on both sides fly strafing runs, escorts and guard patrols.

groups.title: New ship: Silverwing
entries: New starfighter: the Silverwing, a swept-wing strike fighter with twin-barrel cannons on each wingtip. Its guns swivel to track your target, kick back with every shot and glow when they overheat, and its three engines blaze with thrust.

PC: proper fullscreen. The game now starts in borderless fullscreen; press F11 or Alt+Enter to switch any time, or pick Windowed, Fullscreen or Exclusive in Settings › Graphics. Your choice is remembered.

Mouse flying feels like a joystick now: the aim reticle stays where you push it and your ship keeps turning toward it, so you no longer have to keep dragging the mouse. Pull it back to the centre to fly straight, or tap X / middle mouse to snap it home. Deadzone and an optional auto-centre are in Settings › Controls.

groups.title: Star Battles is live
entries: 10 v 10 Conquest around Saturn: capture three relay stations or out-gun the enemy fleet, with AI wingmen filling every empty seat.
Three starfighters with gimbal-mounted cannons, lasers, railguns and lock-on missiles, plus animated engines with boost trails.
Destructible asteroid field: shoot big rocks and they split into hot, tumbling fragments.
Online multiplayer over Wi-Fi or the internet, with a public battle list, plus pilot accounts and cloud saves.
Console-style home screen, full touch, gamepad and keyboard controls, and an in-game updater that shows what's new.
